a.summary: The C01 fix also changes classification for lists where gzip is not the outermost coding, turning a previously pass-through body into an UncheckedIOException, and nothing pins that half.
a.failure_scenario: A buffering CDN that re-encodes and sends `Content-Encoding: gzip, br` over a gzip-then-brotli body used to surface as a JSON parse error on the raw bytes; it now surfaces as `UncheckedIOException: ZipException: Not in GZIP format` from `readBody`. The change of failure mode is unpinned, so a later reviewer simplifying the loop back to "last coding wins" would break nothing in the suite.

b.summary: `header.split(",")` turns an untrusted, provider-sized Content-Encoding value into O(n) String allocations, in the one class that otherwise clamps every untrusted header before letting it size an allocation.
b.failure_scenario: A compromised or buggy provider answers every RPC call with `Content-Encoding: ` followed by ~380 KB of `a,` pairs and a normal small body. Each readBody call now burns ~11 ms of CPU and churns ~13 MB of short-lived objects before deciding the body is not gzip; pre-patch the same header cost a length comparison. At even modest request concurrency that is a self-inflicted allocation storm from a header the client never had to parse token-by-token.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
